title: History traversal and reload: which initiator does the request carry? (follow-up to #4446)

labels.name: compat
labels.description: Standard is not web compatible or proprietary feature needs standardizing

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

This is an attempt at a follow-up @annevk had asked for on #4446, based on https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4446#issuecomment-3666877424 from @terjanq.

#4446 was closed as fixed by #6315, which added the [document state’s initiator origin](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#document-state-initiator-origin). But, nothing uses that initiator origin for the request a traversal or reload makes. So the Origin header, `Sec-Fetch-Site`, and whether the request counts as _“directly user-initiated”_ still come from whichever document the traversal happens to use as its source — **not from the navigation that created the entry.**

### What the spec says now

In [apply the history step](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#apply-the-history-step), a traversal or reload with no source snapshot params of its own snapshots them from the navigable’s active document, with this note:

> In this case there is no clear source of the traversal/reload. We treat this situation as if navigable navigated itself, but note that some properties of targetEntry’s original initiator are preserved in targetEntry’s document state, such as the initiator origin and referrer, which will appropriately influence the navigation.

The referrer does influence it: [create navigation params by fetching](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#create-navigation-params-by-fetching) uses the document state’s request referrer. But the initiator origin only sets the request’s *top-level navigation initiator origin* (step 4). The request’s origin still comes from its client — the active document, or the document that called `history.back()` or `location.reload()`. So, per spec:

- Going back from a cross-site page to one reached by a same-origin link sends `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`.
- Reloading a page reached from another site sends `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`.

Also, [step 19](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#create-navigation-params-by-fetching) gives a redirected entry a new document state with no initiator origin at all — **so a replaying spec would still need a decision for redirected entries.**

### What engines actually do

- **Blink** replays the entry’s initiator for every traversal and reload, browser-initiated or not: `NavigationEntryImpl::ConstructCommonNavigationParams()` passes `frame_entry.initiator_origin()`, and `GetInitiatorRelation()` in `services/network/sec_header_helpers.cc` sends `none` when there’s no initiator — as there isn’t, for an entry the user typed.
- **Gecko** replays the entry’s triggering principal: `SessionHistoryInfo::FillLoadInfo()` sets it on the load state, and `SecFetch.cpp` compares against it — with `IsUserTriggeredForSecFetchSite()` sending `none` when it’s the system principal.
- **WebKit** computes the relation against the document being left, as the spec does: `FrameLoader::loadDifferentDocumentItem()` gives the load’s `NavigationAction` the current document as its requester, and `computeFetchMetadataSite()` uses that requester’s origin. For a non-POST load it passes the main frame’s `lastNavigationWasAppInitiated()` as `isRequestFromClientOrUserInput`, so whether `none` goes out seems to depend on how the current page was reached, rather than on the entry.
- **Ladybird** follows Blink and Gecko: It takes the request’s origin from the entry’s initiator origin, and replays `none` for every traversal and reload.

### The problem with replaying everything

Summary of @terjanq’s https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4446#issuecomment-3666877424: A page the user reaches directly (typed, or opened from a context menu) gets an entry with no initiator. That page opens a popup, which navigates the original window to `about:blank` and then calls `opener.history.back()`. The traversal fetches the page again with the replayed browser-initiated state — and this time the page redirects to a sensitive site.

Since `Sec-Fetch-Site: none` survives redirects (Fetch Metadata’s [set site](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-fetch-metadata/#abstract-opdef-set-site) only walks the URL list when the value isn’t `none`), the sensitive site gets `Sec-Fetch-Site: none` and SameSite=Strict cookies, from a navigation a cross-site page caused.

Various commenters in #4446 favored replaying the initiator so that Back means _“take me back to what I saw”_ — which this report shows can’t extend to replaying browser-initiated state for a traversal a page starts.

### Proposal

1. When fetching a traversal or reload, set the request’s origin from the target entry’s document state’s initiator origin, matching Blink and Gecko — so `Sec-Fetch-Site` and a resubmitted POST’s Origin header go out as they did the first time.
2. Treat the request as directly user-initiated (Fetch Metadata’s step 4 of [set site](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-fetch-metadata/#abstract-opdef-set-site)) only when the traversal or reload itself came from the browser UI; that is, its user navigation involvement is “browser UI”, *and* the entry’s own navigation was directly user-initiated. A page’s `history.back()` or `location.reload()` never replays it.
3. Decide what a redirected entry keeps (step 19 currently drops the initiator origin).

Ladybird implements 1, with an opaque initiator origin left to the current behavior (it’s what a browser-UI navigation records, and it has to keep reaching `file:` URLs). It doesn’t implement 2; for interoperability, it replays `none` for a page-started traversal — as Blink and Gecko do.

For the directly-user-initiated part, https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-fetch-metadata/issues/100 is a companion issue I raised against the Fetch Metadata’s [directly user-initiated requests](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-fetch-metadata/#directly-user-initiated) section.
